title: How to run Pyspark UDF separately over dataframe groups
question:
Grouping a Pyspark dataframe, applying time series analysis UDF to each group

SOLVED See below

I have a Pyspark process which takes a time-series dataframe for a site and calculates/adds features for anomaly detection. Window functions are used to compare leading and lagging reads, and aggregates like mean, median, std deviation are used.

This runs one site at a time, but I would like to run this across a single large dataframe containing data for many sites, applying the functions to each group of the dataframe separately and returning a single modified dataframe.

# Illustrative functions
window = Window.partitionBy("Site").orderBy("DateTime").rowsBetween(-2, 0)
val_mean = df.agg(mean("Value")).collect()[0][0]

df = df.withColumn("NewCol", col("Value") - val_mean)
df = df.withColumn("rolling_mean", avg(col("Value")).over(window))

I've trying to avoid For Loops and Pandas for scalability and parallel processing, but have not found the proper way to do this with PySpark.

What are the options here?

(Running on Azure Databricks, if that matters)

Example desired behavior
Site DateTime Value NewCol rolling_mean
A 04/01/2026 1 -0.8 null
A 05/01/2026 2 -0.2 null
A 06/01/2026 3 1.2 0.2
A 07/01/2026 1 -0.8 0.2
A 08/01/2026 2 0.2 0.2
B 03/01/2026 4 -6.4 null
B 04/01/2026 5 -5.4 null
B 05/01/2026 34 23.6 3.93
B 06/01/2026 5 -5.4 4.26
B 07/01/2026 4 -6.4 3.93

SOLVED

Pandas performance was much worse that than the pure Pyspark implementation and introduced additional execution plan complexity (causing errors on some cluster, e.g. Serverless).

Using "concurrent.futures" allowed existing functions to be applied with minimal adjustment and execution performance was many times faster than the Pandas implementation.

# Divide task across workers
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=4) as executor:  
    results = {executor.submit(anomaly_func, raw_df.filter(raw_df.Id == key)) for key in IdList}

# Union the results dataframe
df = None
for r in results:
    df = r.result()
    if df is None:
        df = df
    else:
        df = df.union(df)
